title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio

reading.body:
The core failure here is a system trained on copyrighted material without authorization from the rights holders. Udio's AI music generator allegedly ingested recordings it had no license to use, and the problem emerged at the training stage, before any user ever generated a song. This is a data-sourcing failure, not a runtime or output-quality failure. It would have required rights clearance at the point of dataset assembly to avoid, which was not done.

The legal consequences span multiple parties. Universal Music Group settled and entered a licensing arrangement with Udio for a new platform. Warner Music Group followed the same path. Sony Music filed a separate lawsuit after a judge declined to allow it to add more than 30,000 recordings to its original case, so Sony brought those recordings as a new action. A class action by independent artists was not dismissed and was moved between jurisdictions. A musicians' union lawsuit over the UMG settlement is also pending.

None of the lawsuits have produced final verdicts on liability, and the settlements reached so far do not constitute admissions of wrongdoing. What is alleged, not established, is that Udio knowingly copied the recordings or that any specific quantity of protected material can be proven to have influenced model outputs.

summary:
# Summary

Universal Music Group has settled a lawsuit against AI music startup Udio with new licensing agreements. UMG had accused Udio of using copyrighted songs to train its artificial intelligence system, including The Temptations' hit "My Girl." Under the settlement, Udio will launch a new platform next year that uses only authorized and licensed music, allowing users to create, customize, stream and share songs. The financial terms were not disclosed.

This settlement marks Udio's first licensing agreement with a major music label and represents a significant step toward resolving disputes between the music industry and AI companies. Udio's CEO stated the collaboration will help redefine how AI supports artists and fans. Artists can choose to opt into the new platform and will receive compensation, though specific details were not provided. UMG also announced a separate partnership with Stability AI to develop music creation tools for artists and producers.
